In linguistics , grammatical mood is a grammatical feature of verbs , used for signaling modality . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] : 181 [ 3 ] In other words, it is the use of verbal inflections that allow speakers to express their attitude toward what they are saying (for example, a statement of fact, of desire, of command, etc.). The term is also used more broadly to describe the syntactic expression of modality – that is, the use of verb phrases that do not involve inflection of the verb itself.
